label: EU(7)-PIM: racecadotril
title: Racecadotril in an older person
statement: Racecadotril | In lists: does not appear as PIM | Main reason: No proven efficacy; selective inhibitor of enkephalinase enzyme responsible for the degradation of the enkephalins, endogenous opioids which act by decreasing the intestinal lumen secretion of water and electrolytes | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Maximum dose 100 mg/8h; maximum duration 7 days. E | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological measures, e.g. diet. E

plain_summary: The EU(7)-PIM panel included racecadotril, a medicine for diarrhoea, because it found no proven benefit in older people. The words “does not appear as PIM” refer to the six earlier lists the authors compared.

medicine_groups.name: Racecadotril
medicine_groups.note: No Australian brand is listed. A history would show the ingredient name.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when a Group A medicine (racecadotril) is supplied, at any dose, to a patient aged 65 years or over. If age is missing and the other requirements are met, report only a possible finding and ask for the patient's age. One supply is enough. A patient aged under 65 years is not a finding.
cannot_be_seen: A dated diagnosis may identify the cause of the diarrhoea. Supplies alone cannot establish the cause, how many days the capsules were taken or whether the patient obtained medicine elsewhere.
ask_the_gp: A review of the cause of the diarrhoea and of whether racecadotril is still needed.
